structured_answers.q1_what_detected: FoodSure AI detected an infrared spectral pattern consistent with pure turmeric powder (0% wheat flour adulteration).
structured_answers.q2_what_it_means: FoodSure AI classified this sample as pure turmeric based on its infrared absorption profile. The continuous regression model estimated an adulteration level of 0.00% (or near-zero). This indicates no detectable wheat flour presence within the model's 7-tier resolution, though this preliminary screening result should be confirmed through accredited laboratory testing.
structured_answers.q3_supporting_evidence: The classification is supported by 2,522 infrared wavenumber measurements (4000 to 650 cm⁻¹) compressed via 91 orthogonal principal components (90.1% explained variance). Key diagnostic absorbance peaks include starch glycosidic C-O-C vibration at 1045.76 cm⁻¹ and wheat gluten peptide Amide I at 1679.21 cm⁻¹.
structured_answers.q4_uncertainties_limitations: The model was evaluated on a controlled 350-sample benchmark dataset using wheat flour as the sole adulterant. The model assigns patterns to seven discrete training tiers (0%, 1%, 2%, 3%, 5%, 7%, 9%) and does not provide calibrated posterior probabilities. Real-world market variation and other adulterants are outside current scope.
structured_answers.q5_what_next: Submit the physical sample to an accredited food testing facility for confirmatory wet-chemistry analysis, specifically AOAC 972.16 polarizing microscopy for wheat starch granules or AOAC 2016.16 HPLC-DAD for curcuminoid assay.

analysis.summary: The FoodSure AI system analyzed an ATR-FTIR spectroscopic fingerprint (sample partition: unknown) using a Logistic Regression classifier supported by principal component analysis (PCA) dimensionality reduction. The model predicted pure turmeric (0% adulteration). The regression estimator independently quantified the adulteration level at approximately 0.00333333%. This is a research-prototype model output and must not be used in place of validated laboratory analysis.
analysis.interpretation: The model predicted class: 0%. This indicates the model believes the sample contains no detectable wheat flour adulteration within the model's seven-class resolution. The Random Forest Regressor provides an independent continuous estimate of 0.00333333%, which may differ from the classifier's discrete class label. Both outputs come from the same spectral features but use different mathematical approaches. The classifier assigns each sample to one of seven discrete adulteration levels; it cannot detect adulteration outside these trained classes. The model does not supply calibrated posterior probabilities, so the output should be interpreted as a pattern-matching decision rather than a statistical confidence score.

structured_answers.q2_what_it_means: FoodSure AI classified this sample as pure turmeric based on its infrared absorption profile. The continuous regression model estimated an adulteration level of 0.00% (or near-zero). This indicates no detectable wheat flour presence within the model's 7-tier resolution, though this preliminary screening result should be confirmed through accredited laboratory testing.
structured_answers.q3_supporting_evidence: The classification is supported by 2,522 infrared wavenumber measurements (4000 to 650 cm⁻¹) compressed via 91 orthogonal principal components (90.1% explained variance). Key diagnostic absorbance peaks include starch glycosidic C-O-C vibration at 1034.35 cm⁻¹ and wheat gluten peptide Amide I at 1667.8 cm⁻¹.
structured_answers.q4_uncertainties_limitations: The model was evaluated on a controlled 350-sample benchmark dataset using wheat flour as the sole adulterant. The model assigns patterns to seven discrete training tiers (0%, 1%, 2%, 3%, 5%, 7%, 9%) and does not provide calibrated posterior probabilities. Real-world market variation and other adulterants are outside current scope.
structured_answers.q5_what_next: Submit the physical sample to an accredited food testing facility for confirmatory wet-chemistry analysis, specifically AOAC 972.16 polarizing microscopy for wheat starch granules or AOAC 2016.16 HPLC-DAD for curcuminoid assay.

explanation_five_sections.what_it_means: This result indicates that the sample's infrared spectrum exhibits absorption patterns characteristic of pure turmeric rhizome without detectable flour additives.
explanation_five_sections.supporting_evidence: Input validation confirmed 2,522 contiguous wavenumber features aligned with the trained PCA representation. Observable absorption at 1034.35 cm⁻¹ (absorbance: 0.7561) reflects polysaccharide content, while absorption at 1490.89 cm⁻¹ corresponds to curcuminoid aromatics.
explanation_five_sections.important_limitations: This model operates as a research screening prototype. The classifier evaluates pattern proximity rather than calibrated statistical certainty. It cannot diagnose adulterants other than wheat flour or replace ISO-certified assays.
explanation_five_sections.recommended_next_step: Treat this screening verdict as an indicator. For commercial release, regulatory filing, or quality disputes, conduct independent laboratory microscopy or HPLC testing.
